subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should QMD upgrades automatically move bare stdio MCPorter definitions to OpenClaw-managed per-agent configuration while leaving customized definitions externally owned?
rationale: This changes existing configuration and daemon ownership in order to fix cross-agent state coupling; tests can validate mechanics, but only maintainers can accept the intended upgrade contract.

options.title: Accept the split after checks
options.body: Land the generated-versus-external policy once the exact head is green, treating bare stdio definitions as safe to regenerate per agent.

options.title: Require broader upgrade proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until live Linux upgrade and Windows path evidence demonstrate both generated and external configurations on the final head.

options.title: Narrow the repair
options.body: Pause this branch and pursue a smaller environment-only fix, accepting that it may not fully isolate QMD child state or daemon ownership.

recommendation.title: Accept the split after checks
recommendation.body: Land the generated-versus-external policy once the exact head is green, treating bare stdio definitions as safe to regenerate per agent.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged QMD/MCPorter routing and compatibility work makes this person the strongest available owner for the upgrade-contract decision.
